problems.title: Probability of exactly one event
problems.question: P(A)=.6, P(B)=.5, P(A∩B)=.3. Find P((A\B)∪(B\A)).
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: $P(A\triangle B)=P(A)+P(B)-2P(A\cap B)$.
steps: The disjoint A-only and B-only probabilities are.3 and.2. Add them.

problems.title: Ten arithmetic terms
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression, a₃=1.2, a₈=3.2. Find the first 10-term sum.

problems.title: Difference from a partial-sum formula
problems.question: Sₙ=3n²+5n is the sum of the first n arithmetic terms. Find the common difference.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
steps: The difference between consecutive linear terms is 6.

problems.title: Collinear vector and dot product
problems.question: a is collinear with b=(−1,2), and a·b=45. Find the coordinate sum of a.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: Write $a=tb$. Then $a\cdot b=t|b|^2=5t$.
steps: t=9, so a=(−9,18). Its coordinate sum is 9.

problems.title: Length of a vector combination
problems.question: a=(1,2), b=(−1,3). Find |a−2b|.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
steps: Its length is √(3²+4²).

problems.title: Standard deviation from a median
problems.question: The data are x,2,−1,3,0 and have median 1. Find their standard deviation.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: The only way the middle observation can be 1 is x=1. The sorted data are −1,0,1,2,3, with mean 1.
steps: Population variance is[(−2)²+(−1)²+0²+1²+2²]/5=10/5=2. Take the square root.

problems.title: A decreasing geometric triple
problems.question: The numbers a+6, a,2a/3 for m a decreasing geometric progression. Find the least integer strictly greater than a.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: The middle-square rule gives $a^2=(a+6)(2a/3)$, hence a(a−12)=0.
steps: a=0 gives 6,0,0, which is not strictly decreasing. At a=12 the triple 18,12,8 has common ratio 2/3. The next integer after 12 is 13.

problems.title: A two-dice sum bound
problems.question: Roll two independent fair dice. Find the probability the sum is at most 9.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: There are 36 equally likely ordered outcomes. The complement sums 10,11,12 have 3,2,1 outcomes.
steps: Subtract 6 from 36 and divide by 36.

problems.title: Codirected vectors
problems.question: For which p are(p,−6) and(−6,4p) codirected?
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: Collinearity gives $4p^2-36=0$, so p=±3. Codirection requires a positive scalar multiplier.
steps: At p=−3, the second vector is 2 times the first. At p=3, it is −2 times the first and points oppositely.

problems.title: Vector of a trapezoid midline
problems.question: M, N are midpoints of trapezoid legs AB, CD. AB=a and AC=b as vectors, and base AD=3BC. Find vector MN.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: With A as origin, B=a, C=b. Then $D=3(b-a)$, $M=a/2$, and $N=(C+D)/2$.
steps: Subtract: N−M=[b+3(b−a)−a]/2=2b−2a.

problems.title: A geometric series and its even terms
problems.question: A convergent geometric series has total sum 4 times the sum of its even-indexed terms. Find its ratio q.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: For nonzero first term t, $S=t/(1-q)$ and $S_{even}=tq/(1-q^2)$, with |q|<1.
steps: S=4S_even gives 1+q=4q, so 3q=1. This ratio is convergent.

problems.title: Relative frequency after deleting observations
problems.question: A data value occurs 3 times in n observations. Delete 5 other values; its relative frequency rises by 1/10. Find n.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
steps: This gives 15/[n(n−5)]=1/10, or n²−5n−150=0. Factor(n−15)(n+10)=0; only 15 is admissible.

problems.title: Maximise an arithmetic-progression expression
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression a₉=1. For which d is a₁₀a₈+a₆a₈+a₆a₁₀ largest?
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
steps: The expression expands to 3−6d−d²=12−(d+3)². Its maximum occurs when d+3=0.

problems.title: Recover an angle from a dot product
problems.question: |a|=1,|b|=2 and(a+2b)·(b−a)=9. Find the angle between a, b.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: The left side expands to $2|b|^2-|a|^2-a\cdot b=7-a\cdot b$.
steps: Thus a·b=−2. Divide by |a||b|=2 to obtain cosθ=−1.

problems.title: Nested regular hexagons
problems.question: Choose a point uniformly inside a regular hexagon. Find the chance it lies in the regular hexagon inscribed in the first hexagon’s incircle.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: The first hexagon circumradius is R; its inradius is $r=R\cos30°=R\sqrt3/2$. Similar polygon areas have the squared radius ratio.
steps: Probability=area_small/area_large=r²/R²=3/4.

problems.title: Two index relations and degenerate progressions
problems.question: An arithmetic progression satisfies aₙ−a₉=a₅−aₘ, and a geometric progression satisfies bₘ/bₙ=b₅/b₁₁. Find n²−m².
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: For nonzero arithmetic difference d, $(n+m-14)d=0$ gives n+m=14. For nonzero geometric ratio with |q|≠1, the quotient equation gives m−n=−6.
steps: These nondegenerate conditions yield n=10, m=4, so n²−m²=(n−m)(n+m)=6·14=84.

However, a constant arithmetic progression need not force n+m=14, and a constant geometric progression or alternating ratio−1 need not force n−m=6. For example, bₖ=(−1)ᵏ with n=m=7 satisfies both displayed equations for any arithmetic progression, but gives 0.
problems.answer: Intended nondegenerate answer:84. As stated, the data are insufficient.
problems.note: The source does not exclude constant progressions or the geometric ratio−1; these cases prevent a unique numerical answer.

problems.title: Two related geometric sums
problems.question: A geometric progression satisfies b₂+b₅−b₄=12 and b₅−b₆−b₃=−6. Find b₉/b₁₂.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: For common ratio q, the second left side is $-q$ times the first, term by term.
steps: Hence −12q=−6, giving q=1/2. The requested ratio is q^(9−12)=q^(−3)=8.

problems.title: Perpendicular line at a given distance
problems.question: A line y=kx+b is perpendicular to x−2y=1 and has distance√5 from the origin. Find √(b²−4k²).
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: The original slope is 1/2, so k=−2. Point-to-line distance is $|b|/\sqrt{1+k^2}$.
steps: Thus |b|/√5=√5, so b²=25. The requested radicand is 25−4·4=9.

problems.title: A convex vector combination
problems.question: Distinct A, B, C, D satisfy DA=.1DC+.9DB as vectors. Find the angle between CA and BA.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: Adding D cancels it out and gives $A=.1C+.9B$.
steps: Thus A lies strictly between B and C. The vectors CA=.9(B−C) and BA=.1(C−B) point oppositely.

problems.title: Angle between two lines in a square
problems.question: Square ABCD has side 2. M is midpoint of CD and BK: KC=1:2 on BC. Find the cosine of the acute angle between AK and BM.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
steps: Direction vectors are u=(2,2/3), v=(−1,2). Their dot product is −2/3. For the acute line angle use the absolute dot product: cosθ=(2/3)/[√(40/9)√5]=2/√200=√2/10.

problems.title: An arithmetic pattern among symmetric roots
problems.question: How many m make the real roots of $x^4-(2m+4)x^2+m^2=0$ for m an arithmetic progression with at least 3 distinct terms?
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: At m=0, the roots are −2,0,2, an arithmetic progression. For m≠0, any such progression among the four symmetric roots must have roots $-3t,-t,t,3t$ with t>0.
steps: Vieta on their squared positive roots gives 10t²=2m+4 and 3t²=|m|. Thus(10/3)|m|=2m+4. If m>0, solve 10m=6m+12, giving m=3. If m<0, solve−10m=6m+12, giving m=−3/4. Both give positive t² and four valid equally spaced roots. Include m=0.

problems.title: Probability of roots beyond both unit bounds
problems.question: Uniformly choose a∈[−9,9]. Find the probability that x²−ax−2=0 has one root≤−1 and the other≥1.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: The product −2 ensures two real roots of opposite signs. For both bounds require $f(-1)=a-1\le0$ and $f(1)=-a-1\le0$.
steps: Thus −1≤a≤1. Its interval length is 2, out of total 18.

problems.title: An integer geometric triple with a prescribed mean
problems.question: Increasing natural x, y, z for m a geometric progression with natural ratio q, and their mean is y+3. Which listed range z−x is possible?
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: Write x=t, y=tq, z=tq² with t≥1, q≥2. The mean condition gives $t(q-1)^2=9$.
steps: The positive square divisors of 9 are 1,9. Thus q=2, t=9 gives range 9(4−1)=27; q=4, t=1 gives range 16−1=15. Only 15 is listed.
problems.answer: Listed range:15. Full possible ranges:15 and 27.

problems.title: Shortest distance from a circle to a line
problems.question: A lies on x²+6x−8y+y²=0 and B on3y=4x−6. Find min AB.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: The circle is $(x+3)^2+(y-4)^2=25$, centre O=(−3,4), radius 5. The line is 4x−3y−6=0.
steps: Its distance from O is|4(−3)−3·4−6|/5=6. The line is outside the circle, so the nearest distance is 6−5.

problems.title: Triangle altitude from two vectors
problems.question: AB=(8,6), BC=(5,−10). Find the altitude from C to AB.
problems.idea: Apply the probability, progression, or vector definition and verify its assumptions.
formulas: The parallelogram determinant magnitude is $|8(-10)-6(5)|=110$. The base length is $|AB|=10$.
steps: The determinant equals base times altitude; using AC=AB+BC gives the same determinant as BC. Hence h=110/10.
